- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show upward trend but true outcome shows downward drift, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid over-leverage.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of true values if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.5, -0.5, +0.5), model tends to lag — add 1–2% buffer to forecast to capture momentum.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 2–5% for next period to avoid “lagging behind”.
